title: Background estimation treats missing zero depths as real floor observations
body:
## Current source and observed behavior

Base inspected: `d1b0e75d0a696d071d4d158ab2b16787f52890df` (`release`). Source: [moseq2_extract/extract/proc.py](https://github.com/dattalab/moseq2-extract/blob/d1b0e75d0a696d071d4d158ab2b16787f52890df/moseq2_extract/extract/proc.py).

A generated 3-frame, 8x8 depth stack has valid depth 700 and zero dropout in two observations of an interior patch. With med_scale=1, get_bground_im_file returns zero for that patch. np.nanmedian does not ignore zero. The pre-temporal spatial blur also spreads invalid depths.

## Narrow reproduction

```python
def test_background_treats_zero_dropout_as_depth(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    from moseq2_extract.extract import proc
    images = np.full((3, 8, 8), 700, dtype=np.uint16)
    images[:2, 2:6, 2:6] = 0
    monkeypatch.setattr(proc.moseq2_extract.io.video, 'load_movie_data', lambda path, idx, **kw: images[idx])
    monkeypatch.setattr(proc, 'write_image', lambda *a, **kw: None)
    value = proc.get_bground_im_file('synthetic-unused', frame_stride=1, med_scale=1,
                                    output_dir=str(tmp_path), finfo={'nframes': 3, 'dims': (8, 8)})
    assert value[3, 3] == 0  # missing zero depths dominate valid 700 mm
```

The generated-fixture diagnostic passed against the installed current-upstream wheel. Its assertion describes the observed defect, not an accepted corrected result.

## Why this is an issue rather than speculative patch code

The right policy for persistently unobserved pixels and spatial/temporal filtering needs an explicit decision. I have not transplanted our project-specific imputation heuristic or proposed a new empirical threshold.

No recordings, fitted scientific artifacts, real genotype/treatment data, PCA/ARHMM fit, or validation outputs were used. This report comes from a historical project-finding reconciliation, not adoption of unrelated notebook xfails. Existing issue/PR descriptions were checked before filing.

title: Automatic floor range can be centered on a missing-depth pixel
body:
## Current source and observed behavior

Base inspected: `d1b0e75d0a696d071d4d158ab2b16787f52890df` (`release`). Source: [moseq2_extract/helpers/wrappers.py](https://github.com/dattalab/moseq2-extract/blob/d1b0e75d0a696d071d4d158ab2b16787f52890df/moseq2_extract/helpers/wrappers.py).

The current automatic-range branch reads bground_im[cY][cX] after get_bucket_center and uses that single value +/-50 mm. A zero/missing center in an otherwise valid synthetic 700 mm floor therefore produces [-50,50]. This is a static branch-level reproduction, not an end-to-end ROI acceptance claim.

## Narrow reproduction

```python
import numpy as np
background = np.full((8,8), 700.)
background[4,4] = 0
value = background[4,4]
assert [int(value-50), int(value+50)] == [-50,50]
```

The snippet isolates the exact current branch behavior; it does not claim full-pipeline reproduction.

## Why this is an issue rather than speculative patch code

A robust floor/arena choice is a broader acquisition-policy decision: a background mode need not be the arena floor. Our historical mode/connected-component heuristic is available in the linked project history but is not offered as a universally correct replacement.

title: Missing physical scalar observations are filled with measured zeros
body:
## Current source and observed behavior

Base inspected: `5b52b176fbfa4fb1a6a7a69f48e7c37ac2730ba8` (`release`). Source: [moseq2_viz/model/stat.py](https://github.com/dattalab/moseq2-viz/blob/5b52b176fbfa4fb1a6a7a69f48e7c37ac2730ba8/moseq2_viz/model/stat.py).

get_session_mean_df fills an unobserved syllable scalar with zero. In a two-session synthetic table where each session expresses only one state, the absent height is returned as 0 rather than missing. Zero usage/count can be meaningful; zero height/duration for an unobserved state is not a measurement. The app InteractiveSyllableStats path separately calls self.df.fillna(0).

## Narrow reproduction

```python
def test_noncount_statistic_missing_values_become_zero():
    from moseq2_viz.model.stat import get_session_mean_df
    frame = pd.DataFrame([
        {'group': 'synthetic-a', 'uuid': 'a', 'syllable': 0, 'height': 50., 'usage': 1.},
        {'group': 'synthetic-b', 'uuid': 'b', 'syllable': 1, 'height': 60., 'usage': 1.}])
    result = get_session_mean_df(frame, statistic='height', max_syllable=2)
    assert result.loc['synthetic-a', 'a'][1] == 0
    assert result.loc['synthetic-b', 'b'][0] == 0
```

The generated-fixture diagnostic passed against the installed current-upstream wheel. Its assertion describes the observed defect, not an accepted corrected result.

## Why this is an issue rather than speculative patch code

A responsible fix needs a consistent missing-data policy through each statistical test and plot, including effective sample counts and Kruskal/permutation handling. Simply deleting fillna can reintroduce the notebook failures addressed in app PR #94. Please do not interpret this report as prescribing Welch, a new family of hypotheses, or a biological conclusion.

title: Held-out sessions affect the training whitening transform
body:
## Current source and observed behavior

Base inspected: `ed1fb9bff59db377eb3b45d996b3195ff0f93637` (`release`). Source: [moseq2_model/helpers/data.py](https://github.com/dattalab/moseq2-model/blob/ed1fb9bff59db377eb3b45d996b3195ff0f93637/moseq2_model/helpers/data.py).

prepare_model_metadata selects held-out keys, then calls whiten_all(data_dict) on the entire input dictionary. A generated two-session example with hold_out_seed=0 holds b out and trains on a. Changing only b shifts the transformed a. No sampler is invoked.

## Narrow reproduction

```python
def test_whitening_training_parameters_depend_on_heldout_values():
    from moseq2_model.helpers.data import prepare_model_metadata
    config = dict(kappa=100, hold_out=True, nfolds=2, hold_out_seed=0, ncpus=1,
                  gamma=1, alpha=1, nlags=1, robust=False, max_states=2,
                  separate_trans=False, whiten='all', noise_level=0)
    def prepare(offset):
        rng = np.random.RandomState(17)
        data = OrderedDict(a=rng.normal(size=(20, 2)),
                           b=rng.normal(size=(20, 2)) + offset)
        return prepare_model_metadata(data, {'groups': {'a': 'synthetic', 'b': 'synthetic'}}, dict(config))
    first, second = prepare(100), prepare(1000)
    assert first[2] == second[2] == ['a']
    assert first[3] == second[3] == ['b']
    assert not np.array_equal(first[0]['a'], second[0]['a'])
```

The generated-fixture diagnostic passed against the installed current-upstream wheel. Its assertion describes the observed defect, not an accepted corrected result.

## Why this is an issue rather than speculative patch code

If the intended evaluation is inductive held-out validation, preprocessing parameters must be estimated from training data and applied to held-out data. If transductive preprocessing is intentional, that limitation needs explicit documentation. A coherent implementation must also settle whiten-each/unseen-session behavior, temporal percent splits, and saved transform compatibility; I have not guessed those policies.

No recordings, fitted scientific artifacts, real genotype/treatment data, PCA/ARHMM fit, or validation outputs were used. This report comes from a historical project-finding reconciliation, not adoption of unrelated notebook xfails. Existing issue/PR descriptions were checked before filing.

title: Define a migration/rejection policy for the mixed-unit velocity_3d_px scalar
body:
## Current source and observed behavior

Base inspected: `5b52b176fbfa4fb1a6a7a69f48e7c37ac2730ba8` (`release`). Source: [moseq2_viz/scalars/util.py](https://github.com/dattalab/moseq2-viz/blob/5b52b176fbfa4fb1a6a7a69f48e7c37ac2730ba8/moseq2_viz/scalars/util.py).

The legacy converter constructs velocity_3d_px by summing squared x/y pixel displacements and squared height_ave_mm differences. get_scalar_triggered_average also accepts this field at its public include_keys boundary without a unit warning or rejection. The attached generated-value test confirms current acceptance. The dimensional defect is not a statement that an arbitrary supplied array is corrupt.

## Narrow reproduction

```python
def test_public_scalar_average_accepts_invalid_mixed_units():
    from moseq2_viz.scalars.util import get_scalar_triggered_average
    result = get_scalar_triggered_average({'synthetic': {'velocity_3d_px': np.arange(12.)}},
                                        {'synthetic': np.tile([0, 0, 1, 1], 3)},
                                        include_keys=['velocity_3d_px'], max_syllable=2, nlags=1)
    assert 'velocity_3d_px' in result
```

The generated-fixture diagnostic passed against the installed current-upstream wheel. Its assertion describes the observed defect, not an accepted corrected result.

## Why this is an issue rather than speculative patch code

Extract now has a focused proposal to stop emitting this invalid field. Existing files and consumers still need a deliberate compatibility policy across public plotting, statistics, embedding and conversion APIs. Our historical fork guards and mapping-preserving filter are project-specific implementations, not an already-existing upstream contract. A warning/deprecation/rejection choice belongs with maintainers.

title: Missing heatmaps are replaced by plausible all-zero images
body:
## Current source and observed behavior

Base inspected: `eefa3d5c15e21adef6e9ede343f2705f37d3e47b` (`release`). Source: [moseq2_app/viz/controller.py](https://github.com/dattalab/moseq2-app/blob/eefa3d5c15e21adef6e9ede343f2705f37d3e47b/moseq2_app/viz/controller.py).

CrowdMovieComparison.generate_crowd_movie_divs catches every Exception while fetching a group PDF, substitutes np.zeros((50,50)), and then passes it to get_pdf_plot whenever cm_path is nonempty. Thus missing data and even unexpected errors can become a normal-looking heatmap. This is confirmed by static inspection and an isolated exception-branch reconstruction, not by opening any movie or running a notebook.

## Narrow reproduction

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
try:
    pd.Series([], dtype=object).iloc[0]
except Exception:
    pdf = np.zeros((50,50))
assert pdf.shape == (50,50) and not pdf.any()
```

The snippet isolates the exact current branch behavior; it does not claim full-pipeline reproduction.

## Why this is an issue rather than speculative patch code

The UI should distinguish not-observed from a measured zero image and should not hide unrelated exceptions. Skipping the whole panel versus rendering an explicit unavailable panel affects how an existing movie remains accessible; I have left that UI/missingness decision open rather than silently dropping evidence.
